pr_title: vd_lavc: let the user provide a priority list of hwdecs to consider
pr_body:
Today, the only way to make mpv consider multiple hwdecs and pick the first one that works is to use one of the `auto` modes. But the list that is considered in those cases is hard-coded. If the user wants to provide their own list, they are out of luck.

And I think that there is now a significant reason to support this - the new Vulkan hwdec is definitely not ready to be in the auto list, but if you want to use it by default, it will not work with many codecs that are normally hardware decodable (only h.264, hevc and av1 if you are very lucky). Everything else will fall back to software decoding.

Instead, what you really want to say is: use Vulkan for whatever it supports, and fall back to my old hwdec for everything else.

One side-effect of this implementation is that you can freely mix hwdec names and special values like `auto` and `no`. The behaviour will be correct, so I didn't try and prohibit any combinations. However, some combinations will be silly - eg: sticking any further values after `no` will result in them being ignored. On the other hand, a combination like `vulkan,auto` could be very useful as that will use Vulkan if possible, and if not, run the normal auto routine.

Fixes #11797
pr_comments:
Would it be possible to allow ctrl-h to swap between the provided list and no, or cycle through the each item in the list somehow? Currently it just swaps between vaapi and no. Of course it's trivial to override it in input.conf, but maybe it could be automated?

Also setting hwdec=no prints this message `Unsupported hwdec: no`

issue_context.title: please Implement hwdec priority fallback
issue_context.body:
Depending on dedicated GPU being used in OS or lower performance integrated GPU instead, the setting needs to change.

Something like hwdec=nvdec/nvdec-copy/cuda/cuda-copy/d3d11va/d3d11va-copy would be really helpful.

Thanks, regards.
comments: Which usecase would this satisfy that `hwdec=auto-safe` or `auto-copy-safe` doesn't?

The use-case I have been thinking of implementing is being able to dynamically fallback if the chosen hwdec doesn't support the video format. So that you can prefer `vulkan` but fall back to `nvdec/d3d11va` for the unsupported formats - which is most of them. I don't know if that's what @StacktraceException was imagining. 

If you just care about detection, then yes, `auto` should be good enough.

> Which usecase would this satisfy that `hwdec=auto-safe` or `auto-copy-safe` doesn't?

the  "auto-safe" is automatic or random, is it not? nvdec is more preferrable than cuda for example.  **User provided priority list is much more specifically tuned to his/her configuration with its order** than some random or stock/default preprogrammed choice order, which often may offer less fps performance than user's tested choices. This is even more important when wanting to use most demanding/advanced post processing profiles (like for each kind of resolution etc).



(Also in case auto-safe does not work then someone may want auto-copy-safe at least (if this isn't covered by just the "auto" option), but the manual does not make this clear…

review_comments: not sure why this is even here but equals empty string should be obsolete with this change

It was there because you could explicitly set the value to the empty string and that was supposed to mean `auto`. I expected that setting the config to the empty string now would result in an empty string list, but it seems to produce a string list with one member and that member is the empty string, which means this handling continues to be necessary.

In fact, if you include a trailing comma, or two commas next to each other, you produce empty string list members.
